role: Business Intelligence Engineer, ROW Supply Chain Analytics
responsibilities: You will design, develop and establish KPIs to monitor analysis and provide strategic insights to drive growth and performance.

You will build infrastructure and implement maintenance strategy for internal datasets to support swift analysis to answer critical business questions. You have the freedom to define data extraction tools and dashboards the team should acquire provided you can justify the cost (Amazon frugality!).
You will work with large data sets, automate data extraction, and build monitoring/reporting dashboards and high value, self-service automated BI solutions
Responsible for up skilling team data management and analytical capabilities by mentoring program managers, junior/peer analysts
You will perform complex data analysis (root cause deep dives, correlations, regressions, simulations, optimization) to identify different opportunities and set priorities to improve them.

You will own end-to-end program management. You will not only develop insights but devise realistic plans and work with key stakeholders (software managers, product managers, retail business managers, sellers, transportation planners/managers, and warehouse managers ) to execute them.

You will be responsible for achieving XX million $ actual savings on the bottom line or adding YY million $ to top line. You will not be responsible for only "recommendation" but actual improvements made to bottom or top line.
You will engage with senior leadership on drafting proposals for new concepts, improvement plans, 3-year strategy and outlook.

You will be a subject matter expert in best in class supply chain optimization policies at Amazon. You will understand intricate details of our fulfillment and ordering systems along with their impact on ground-level

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Speed phrases ("rapidly prototype and deliver solutions", "thrive in fast-paced environments", "quickly approach large ambiguous problems", "swift analysis") dominate with no testing or governance language, so velocity.
evidence.domain_risk: drive real impact on Amazon's long-term profitability
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The role is measured on savings and growth ("actual savings on the bottom line"), but errors affect supply chain decisions rather than financial reporting or compliance, so moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: program managers; software developers; research scientists; product managers; transportation; operations; finance; category; delivery experience; platform (software) teams; retail business managers; sellers; warehouse managers
evidence.data_team_maturity: As part of Amazon's Supply Chain & Analytics
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A named analytics team inside a large supply chain organisation with research scientists and several BIEs being hired implies an established, specialised function.
evidence.jd_authorship: We are NOT a reporting team and we are not looking for reporting analysts.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The responsibilities name concrete methods and counterparts ("root cause deep dives, correlations, regressions, simulations, optimization", "transportation planners/managers"), so a hiring manager wrote them.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: work with key stakeholders (software managers, product managers, retail business managers, sellers, transportation planners/managers, and warehouse managers ) to execute them
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The audience spans supply chain operations, retail, product and finance with no single function dominant, so mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: You will own end-to-end program management.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns programs, sets priorities and drafts "3-year strategy and outlook" with senior leadership, so strategic.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tools or AI-facing data work appear in the posting.
evidence.testing_framing: No testing or data quality signal.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Monitoring here means program KPIs, and no testing or data quality practice is named.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The posting is framed around savings, growth and new concepts, with no reliability or compliance concern.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: We conduct new analysis from ground up, proposing new concepts and technology to meet business needs
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The dominant verbs are build, propose and design new concepts and infrastructure, so greenfield.
ats_keywords: data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines
Statistical Analysis packages such as R, SAS and Matlab
